label: Wells's heat-ray
detail: The Martians of The War of the Worlds use an invisible heat-ray.

label: Einstein describes stimulated emission
detail: A paper on the quantum theory of radiation in Physikalische Zeitschrift sets out absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission.

label: The maser gets its name
detail: Townes names the ammonia maser built at Columbia with Gordon and Zeiger.

label: Gould's notebook coins LASER
detail: Gordon Gould's notarized notebook holds the first recorded use of the acronym.

label: Schawlow and Townes publish the optical maser
detail: Their Physical Review paper proposes a laser with mirrors at each end.

label: The 'death ray' headline
detail: Maiman's ruby laser at Hughes is called a death ray by a newspaper.

label: Lasers enter manufacturing
detail: TWI dates industrial laser use to the 1960s.

label: First laser works
detail: Theodore Maiman and Irnee d'Haenens see laser action from a ruby crystal at Hughes Research Laboratories.

label: First working laser
detail: Theodore Maiman and Irnee d'Haenens see laser action in ruby at Hughes Research Laboratories.

label: First helium-neon laser
detail: Javan, Bennett and Herriott at Bell Labs run the first gas laser and first continuous beam, at 1.15 micrometers.

label: First continuous gas laser
detail: Javan, Bennett and Herriott run a helium-neon laser at Bell Labs at 1,153 nm infrared.

label: First laser treatment of a patient
detail: Charles J. Campbell destroys a retinal tumor with one ruby laser pulse at Columbia-Presbyterian, New York.

label: Red helium-neon line
detail: White and Rigden at Bell Labs get the 632.8 nm red line.

label: First diode laser lases at GE
detail: Robert Hall's team pulses a gallium arsenide diode above 12 A; IBM and MIT Lincoln Lab follow within weeks.

label: Nobel Prize for the maser-laser principle
detail: Townes, Basov and Prokhorov share the Physics prize.

label: Nd:YAG laser at Bell Labs
detail: Neodymium-doped YAG lases at 1.06 micrometers.

label: Patel's nitrogen-CO2 laser
detail: The first gas laser to produce high power continuously, per Lemelson-MIT.

label: Argon-ion laser first seen
detail: William Bridges observes argon-ion lasing at Hughes; krypton lines follow that July. These gas lasers make colored shows possible.

label: Argon-ion laser
detail: William Bridges sees the 488 nm blue line at Hughes Research Labs.

label: Kao's fiber calculation
detail: Charles Kao works out that very pure glass fiber could carry light more than 100 km.

label: Leon Goldman's first laser surgery
detail: The dermatologist later called the father of laser surgery performs his first laser operation.

label: Rockne Krebs shows laser beams as sculpture
detail: "Sculpture Minus Object" at the Washington Gallery of Modern Art used red beams, fog and mirrors.

label: Rockne Krebs shows laser sculpture
detail: "Sculpture Minus Object" in Washington uses red beams, fog and mirrors. Other accounts date his first laser work to 1968.

label: First laser-guided bomb
detail: The US Air Force combat-evaluates the Texas Instruments BOLT-117.

label: Radiation Control for Health and Safety Act
detail: Public Law 90-602 puts radiation-emitting products, lasers included, under federal control.

label: First lunar retroreflector
detail: Apollo 11 leaves a panel of 100 corner cubes on the Moon for laser ranging.

label: Audio/Video/Laser at Mills College
detail: Lowell Cross, David Tudor and Carson Jeffries stage what Cross calls the first multi-color laser light show with x-y scanning.

label: Krebs files a laser art patent
detail: US patent 3,622,228, which ILDA calls apparently the first patent for laser artistic display.

label: First excimer laser
detail: A xenon dimer laser runs at the Lebedev Institute in Moscow.

label: Argon photocoagulator goes on sale
detail: Coherent begins marketing a slit-lamp argon laser for the retina.

label: Pepsi Pavilion opens at Expo '70
detail: A four-color krypton laser system by Cross and Jeffries runs in Osaka; Cross gives the dedication date as March 15.

label: Laser printing at PARC
detail: Starkweather builds SLOT on a Xerox 7000 copier; laser printing is shown at one page per second.

label: Dragon's Jaw falls
detail: Laser-guided bombs bring down the Thanh Hoa and Paul Doumer bridges.

label: New York regulates lasers
detail: Industrial Code Rule 50 takes effect, ahead of the US federal laser standard.

label: Laserium opens at Griffith Observatory
detail: Ivan Dryer's laser show opens in Los Angeles and runs there for nearly three decades.

label: Laserium opens at Griffith Observatory
detail: Ivan Dryer's live-played laser show begins a trial run in Los Angeles and stays 28 years.

label: First UPC scan
detail: A pack of Juicy Fruit gum is scanned by a Spectra-Physics helium-neon scanner in Troy, Ohio.

label: US laser performance standard published
detail: FDA's final rule (40 FR 32256), proposed in 1974, creates the standard now at 21 CFR 1040.10 and 1040.11.

label: Led Zeppelin photographed with lasers
detail: Three beams at Nassau Coliseum, New York - the earliest dated evidence of lasers at a rock show.

label: The Who's argon laser at Leicester
detail: A 4 W argon laser fanned through a diffraction grating at Granby Halls.

label: Moving-magnet galvo patented
detail: The design became practical with neodymium magnets in the late 1980s and reached production in 1992.

label: Xerox 9700
detail: Xerox launches the 9700 laser printer.

label: FDA Laser Notice 22
detail: Light shows fall under the federal standard and show producers count as manufacturers. FDA pages date it November 22 or 23.

label: Lovelight, the first automated show
detail: A planetarium laser show run from stored images and recorded control tracks, with no live player.

label: "Lovelight" runs from stored images
detail: Described by LaserFX as the first automated laser show: images drawn on a digitizing pad and stored in PROMs, control tracks on an 8-track recorder.

label: Gould wins his first basic laser patent
detail: US 4,053,845 on optically pumped laser amplifiers issues after a long fight.

label: "Icarus" on steam screens
detail: Laser images projected onto steam screens over Washington DC in summer 1978.

label: Time reports FDA inspectors at light shows
detail: The Bureau of Radiological Health had told Blue Oyster Cult to adjust its show and halted a preview on the Mall in Washington.

label: Metal-ceramic ion tubes
detail: Coherent introduces Innova tubes, lifting tube life from about 1,500 hours toward 5,000.

label: Jarre plays the laser harp in China
detail: Five concerts in Beijing and Shanghai, on a harp ordered from Bernard Szajner; 218,000 attended by the artist's figure.

label: The turkey experiment
detail: IBM's Srinivasan, Wynne and Blum ablate turkey cartilage with an excimer laser.

label: Stone Mountain laser show opens
detail: The Georgia park's mountain-side show begins; the park estimated 20 million viewers in its first 25 years.

label: Selective photothermolysis
detail: Parrish and Anderson publish the idea in Science that makes targeted skin lasers possible.

label: Stone Mountain Lasershow begins
detail: A mountain face in Georgia becomes a laser screen about 400 ft square.

label: Chirped pulse amplification
detail: Mourou and Strickland publish the method behind petawatt lasers.

label: 21 CFR 1040.11(c) takes its current form
detail: The demonstration laser rule names Classes I, IIa, II and IIIa (50 FR 33702).

label: Pangolin's first product, Laser PC
detail: The company's About page gives 1986 for its founding; another company page says 1985.

label: Rendez-vous Houston
detail: Jarre uses downtown skyscrapers as screens; attendance is estimated at 1.3 million or 1.5 million.

label: ILDA founded
detail: The International Laser Display Association holds its first organizational meeting at Lake Tahoe, Nevada.

label: ILDA founded
detail: The International Laser Display Association holds its first organizational meeting in Lake Tahoe.

label: US manual-reset rule
detail: Class IV laser systems made after this date must need a manual reset after an interlock trip or a power loss over 5 seconds.

label: Optical tweezers hold bacteria
detail: Ashkin captures living bacteria with focused laser light without harming them.

label: Gould's royalties begin
detail: His fourth basic laser patent is approved in April.

label: ILDA Awards begin
detail: The trade association starts its annual awards program.

label: First laser vision correction
detail: The first corrective laser eye surgery on a sighted person.

label: First ILDA DB-25 specification
detail: Later superseded by the ISP-DB25 section of the ILDA Standard Projector.

label: PCAOM and the Cambridge 6800
detail: The polychromatic acousto-optic modulator and Cambridge Technology's 6800 galvo both arrive.

label: ILDA test pattern adopted
detail: The circle-in-square pattern becomes the common way to tune and rate scanners.

label: Pink Floyd tours with copper-vapor lasers
detail: The US tour carried two complete 50 W copper-vapor laser systems built by Oxford Lasers.

label: LD2000 and Phoenix
detail: Pangolin dates Lasershow Designer 2000 with QM2000 hardware to 1995; development of Phoenix Showcontroller began the same year.

label: First refractive excimer approval
detail: FDA approves the Summit Technology excimer laser system (PMA P910067).

label: ILDA Test Pattern revision 002
detail: The published standard sets tuning at 12,000 or 30,000 points per second.

label: ILDA Test Pattern Rev. 002
detail: The circle-in-a-square tuning frame, at 12,000 or 30,000 points per second.

label: Blinding lasers banned
detail: Protocol IV to the CCW is adopted in Vienna.

label: Protocol IV adopted
detail: Vienna adopts the protocol on blinding laser weapons; it enters into force on July 30, 1998.

label: HSE publishes HS(G)95
detail: UK guidance on display laser safety, published in October to replace note PM19 of 1980; since withdrawn.

label: Lidar speed readings admitted
detail: A New Jersey court finds the LTI Marksman 20-20 laser speed detector reasonably reliable, with conditions.

label: First LASIK laser approval
detail: FDA approves the Kremer Excimer Laser System (PMA P970005). IBM's history says 1997.

label: O'Hagan thesis
detail: A Loughborough University PhD on entertainment laser risk finds audience scanning not acceptable as then practiced.

label: Scanners pass 50 kpps
detail: A modified Cambridge 6800 shows the test pattern at 52,083 points per second at 6 degrees.

label: ILDA Standard Projector Rev. 002
detail: Clarified signal levels and interlock on the DB-25 connector.

label: FDA Laser Notice 51
detail: Projectors may be delivered only to customers holding an approved variance.

label: Photon 999 opens at Guggenheim Bilbao
detail: Hiro Yamagata's installation projected 15 lasers onto a structure on the museum facade until December 2.

label: First OPSL ships
detail: Coherent sells a 488 nm optically pumped semiconductor laser as an ion-laser replacement.

label: Last Laserium show at Griffith
detail: "Laser Visions" plays to a sold-out dome; the observatory's timeline gives January 6, the day the building closed.

label: First multicolor laser moving head
detail: LOBO dates its ZAPHIR, a scanned laser in a moving-head fixture, to this year.

label: GE starts the printed LEAP fuel nozzle
detail: Development of the laser powder bed fuel nozzle begins.

label: Plug-in RGB
detail: 5 W full-color DPSS lasers that run from a standard outlet are on offer.

label: First laser mouse
detail: Logitech's MX 1000 ships with Agilent's laser sensor.

label: Roger Waters adds a solid-state laser prism
detail: Five direct-diode solid-state lasers totaling over 100 W drew a rotating 3D prism above the stage.

label: First cleared laser hair-growth device
detail: FDA clears the first low-level light device for male pattern hair loss.

label: FDA Laser Notice 55
detail: Streamlined yearly renewal for eligible show variances; audience scanning excluded.

label: QuickShow and FB3QS
detail: Pangolin's entry software with a USB DAC (maker's date).

label: Aquamarine festival eye injuries
detail: Festivalgoers in Kirzhach, Russia, are treated for retinal injuries after a July laser show; reports give 12, 29 or more than 30 patients.

label: Australia restricts pointer imports
detail: Hand-held laser pointers above 1 mW become prohibited imports, treated as weapons.

label: Global Rainbow first shown
detail: Yvette Mattern's seven parallel laser beams, one per color of the spectrum, debut in New York.

label: Blue diodes reach hobbyists
detail: 445 nm laser diodes pulled from Casio data projectors were sold on at about $46 each, by one hobbyist's account.

label: Airborne Laser hits a rocket
detail: The YAL-1A destroys a boosting test rocket off California.

label: Super Bowl XLIV halftime lasers
detail: Laser Design Productions ran 16 LDP 10 projectors, more than 400 W, for The Who in Miami.

label: Chicago admits lidar evidence
detail: Judge Eileen Burke rules lidar speed evidence admissible in Chicago Traffic Court.

label: BEYOND
detail: Pangolin's flagship show software (maker's date).

label: Airborne Laser retired
detail: The 747 makes its last ferry flight to the Davis-Monthan boneyard.

label: Lasering an aircraft becomes a federal crime
detail: 18 U.S.C. 39A, added by the FAA Modernization and Reform Act, sets a maximum of five years.

label: 18 U.S.C. 39A
detail: Aiming a laser pointer at an aircraft becomes a US federal crime under Public Law 112-95.

label: Tupac "hologram" at Coachella
detail: A 2D projection reflected off a slanted transparent film - Pepper's ghost; the vendor's CEO said it was not holographic.

label: ASML agrees to buy Cymer
detail: About EUR 1.95 billion for the excimer and EUV source maker (reported).

label: Green diodes take over
detail: Laserworld dates the show industry's switch from DPSS green to direct green diodes to this year.

label: FDA proposes IEC harmonization
detail: Docket FDA-2011-N-0070 would incorporate much of IEC 60825-1 and limit toy lasers to Class 1.

label: EDC Kinetic Field, 30+ laser systems
detail: Lasertainment ran RTI NANO and PIKO projectors on the main stage.

label: FB4 and IDTF Rev. 011
detail: Pangolin's network DAC (maker's date); ILDA's .ild file format reaches Revision 011 on November 16.

label: Fourteen-year laser-strike sentence
detail: Sergio Patrick Rodriguez is sentenced in Fresno for aiming a laser pointer at a police helicopter; prosecutors say it is believed to be the longest sentence in a laser-strike case.

label: FDA toy laser guidance
detail: CDRH issues final guidance on minimizing risk from children's toy lasers.

label: Seoul club case report
detail: Clinical Ophthalmology publishes two retinal injuries after a club laser show; both patients recovered after surgery.

label: LaWS at sea
detail: The US Navy announces its laser weapon operated on USS Ponce in the Persian Gulf.

label: Ultra Miami, seven stages of lasers
detail: LaserNet ran over 30 projectors above 20 W each at Bayfront Park.

label: Fiber outsells CO2 for cutting
detail: First year fiber cutting lasers outsold CO2 (reported).

label: IDN adopted
detail: ILDA members vote in Dubai to adopt the IDN Stream specification for laser data over networks.

label: LIGO detects gravitational waves
detail: Two black holes of 36 and 29 solar masses merge about 1.3 billion light-years away.

label: Glowforge crowdfunding
detail: $27.9 million in sales in 30 days (reported).

label: SMILE approved
detail: FDA approves the Zeiss VisuMax femtosecond laser (PMA P150040).

label: Ninth Circuit affirms 60 months
detail: After a 2015 appeal vacated his conviction on a second charge, the court affirms Rodriguez's 60-month sentence under 39A.

label: PROWL results
detail: FDA-led studies report 43-46% new visual symptoms at three months and 1-2% dissatisfied with the surgery.

label: Nordic regulators on audience scanning
detail: The Nordic radiation safety authorities jointly recommended avoiding audience exposure to high-power lasers.

label: FDA Safety Communication on show projectors
detail: FDA recommends against using two brands of projector it says were not sold under an approved variance.

label: 314-fixture Guinness record
detail: ER Productions ran 314 laser fixtures at 1,377 W outside the Las Vegas Convention Center during LDI.

label: Dubai Light Up 2018
detail: A laser and light show on the Burj Khalifa replaced fireworks and set a Guinness record of 109,252 square meters.

label: Djibouti protest
detail: The Pentagon says US aircraft were lased in Djibouti and demarches China.

label: UK Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act in force
detail: Shining a laser at a vehicle's operator carries up to five years and an unlimited fine.

label: Lasers as lighting fixtures
detail: PLSN describes the push to run scanned lasers from standard lighting consoles like any other fixture.

label: Nobel for optical tweezers and chirped pulse amplification
detail: Ashkin, Mourou and Strickland share the Physics prize.

label: TRUMPF describes its EUV drive laser
detail: Five amplifier stages, mean pulse power above 30 kW.

label: Mexico City swaps fireworks for lasers
detail: New Year's Eve fireworks were replaced with a concert and laser show on Reforma Avenue, for air-pollution reasons.

label: Glastonbury headliner laser rigs
detail: ER Productions rigs for Stormzy, Tame Impala, the Chemical Brothers and Hot Chip.

label: 10 petawatts
detail: ELI-NP in Romania fires its first 10 PW pulses.

label: PLASA display laser guidance
detail: PLASA publishes the guide HSE now points to in place of HS(G)95.

label: LiGHT trial
detail: 74.2% of patients treated first with SLT need no glaucoma drops at three years.

label: 642-beam record
detail: Image Engineering set a Guinness record with 642 laser beams at Staples Center, Los Angeles.

label: Canada restricts hand-held lasers
detail: SOR/2020-124 is registered, banning hand-held lasers over 1 mW near airports and in three metro regions.

label: Lidar in a phone
detail: Apple announces the iPhone 12 Pro and Pro Max with a LiDAR Scanner.

label: xTool D1 launches
detail: The desktop engraver that started xTool (reported).

label: DGUV Information 203-036
detail: Germany's accident insurers issue the January 2021 edition of their show laser guidance.

label: MadLaser beta
detail: garageCube adds laser output to the MadMapper world.

label: FAA Advisory Circular 70-1B
detail: The FAA's current outdoor laser guidance, with a change dated May 5, 2022.

label: FAA Advisory Circular 70-1B
detail: Current FAA guidance on outdoor laser operations; Change 1 followed on May 5, 2022.

label: P-8A lased
detail: Australia says a PLA-Navy ship lit up an RAAF P-8A Poseidon with a laser.

label: LASIK labeling draft
detail: FDA issues draft guidance recommending a patient decision checklist and images of possible visual symptoms.

label: HELIOS delivered
detail: Lockheed Martin delivers HELIOS to the destroyer USS Preble.

label: UK recall of Vevor laser engravers
detail: Plug pins below the 6.22 mm minimum; shock risk rated serious.

label: Fusion ignition
detail: NIF gets 3.15 MJ of fusion energy from 2.05 MJ of laser energy.

label: Record year for FAA laser reports
detail: Pilots report 13,304 laser incidents, the highest on the FAA's table.

label: 150,000 OPSLs
detail: Coherent reports more than 150,000 OPSLs in the field.

label: Laser Notice 56
detail: FDA says it does not intend to enforce matching US requirements for products meeting identified IEC 60825-1 Ed. 3 clauses.

label: Stone Mountain's classic show ends
detail: The 40-year laser show is replaced by one with lasers, fireworks and drones.

label: Flagstaff replaces July 4 fireworks
detail: The Arizona city ran a free laser show set to music, citing extreme fire risk.

label: Laser-source searchlight reported
detail: Claypaky's Skylos uses a 300 W white laser source; the maker claims output equal to a 4,000 W xenon lamp.

label: Laser video from deep space
detail: DSOC on Psyche peaks at 267 Mbit/s with an ultra-high-definition video downlink.

label: FDA on laser toys
detail: FDA says laser pointers are not toys and toys should stay within IEC Class 1.

label: Illenium at SoFi Stadium
detail: 147 laser systems totaling more than 4,000 W, by the software maker's account.

label: Lasers on the Eiffel Tower
detail: The Paris 2024 opening ceremony used lasers on the tower.

label: UK rejects Creality Falcon2 at the border
detail: 22 W Class 4 engraver found excessively strong for consumer use; goggles inadequate.

label: Canada rewrites its laser product rules
detail: SOR/2024-196 builds a broad standard on IEC 60825-1 Ed. 3.0, in force a year later.

label: FDA withdraws Laser Notice No. 50
detail: Makers move to Laser Notice No. 56.

label: Coachella and Stagecoach lasers
detail: Polar Productions lit six Coachella stages and brought lasers to Stagecoach for the first time.

label: Olympic lasers at Disneyland Paris
detail: Disney Tales of Magic reused the Eiffel Tower lasers from the opening ceremony.

label: IPG reports 2024 revenue of $977.1 million
detail: Down 24% from 2023 (official).

label: NIF record yield
detail: 8.6 MJ from 2.08 MJ of laser energy, a gain of 4.13.

label: Israel claims laser kills
detail: Israel says lasers downed about 40 drones in combat; which system did it is disputed.

label: 1,100-source Guinness record
detail: Verknipt ArenA at the Johan Cruijff ArenA, Amsterdam, set the current largest laser show record with 1,100 laser emission sources.

label: TRUMPF reports FY2024/25 sales of €4.3 billion
detail: Down about 17% (preliminary).

label: Glowforge restarts under its co-founders
detail: After an Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors.

label: DragonFire contract
detail: The UK MOD reports 650 km/h drones downed and a GBP 316 million contract.

label: Iron Beam handed over
detail: Israel's Ministry of Defense delivers the first combat-ready Iron Beam to the IDF.

label: 49ers laser halftime
detail: An eight-minute laser halftime show at Levi's Stadium by Image Engineering.

label: xTool HKEX listing application made public
detail: Prospectus reports 2024 revenue of RMB 2,475.9 million.

label: FAA reports 2025 laser strikes
detail: 10,994 strikes on aircraft in 2025, down 14% from 2024; the record is 13,304 in 2023.

label: Vivid Sydney's first laser show
detail: Laser Lightfall by ER Productions ran 23 nights at Cockle Bay.

label: FDA revises its laser import alert
detail: Import Alert 95-04, first issued in December 1997, covers laser pointers and light show projectors from listed firms.

label: ILDA Awards in Salzburg
detail: Visual Sensation won the festival category; a Swedish New Year's Eve show won Corporate.
